_meta.indication: Treatment of seizures associated with Dravet syndrome in patients 2 years of age and older taking clobazam; no clinical data support use as monotherapy.

pivotal_trials.phase: Pivotal, category 1 study (phase not otherwise specified)
pivotal_trials.design: Multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group, fixed-dose (50 mg/kg) add-on to clobazam and sodium valproate
pivotal_trials.population: Refractory Dravet syndrome patients ages 3 to 18 years taking clobazam and valproate, with at least 4 generalized clonic or tonic-clonic seizures per month
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Proportion of responders (>=50% reduction in monthly seizure frequency from baseline; treatment success/failure)
pivotal_trials.result: Responder rate 71% for stiripentol vs 5% on placebo (p = 0.0003)

pivotal_trials.phase: Pivotal, category 1 study (phase not otherwise specified)
pivotal_trials.design: Multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group, fixed-dose (50 mg/kg) add-on to clobazam and sodium valproate; stopped prematurely
pivotal_trials.population: Refractory Dravet syndrome patients ages 3 to 18 years taking clobazam and valproate, with at least 4 generalized clonic or tonic-clonic seizures per month
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Proportion of responders (>=50% reduction in monthly seizure frequency from baseline; treatment success/failure)
pivotal_trials.result: Responder rate 67% for stiripentol vs 9% on placebo (p = 0.006; significance nominal because study stopped prematurely)

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (>=10% and more than placebo): somnolence, decreased appetite, agitation, ataxia, weight decreased, hypotonia, nausea, tremor, dysarthria, insomnia. Somnolence 67% vs 23% placebo; decreased appetite 46% vs 10%; decreased weight 27% vs 6%; neutropenia 13% (none on placebo); thrombocytopenia 12% vs 3%.
target_moa: Precise anticonvulsant mechanism unknown; thought to act by potentiation of GABAergic (and possibly glutamatergic) neurotransmission, with indirect effects via inhibition of cytochrome P450 activity.
modality: Small molecule (aromatic allylic alcohol / pentanol derivative)

advisory_committee.vote: Not referred to an advisory committee because the safety profile of stiripentol is acceptable for the proposed indication.

description.text: Expanded indication for seizures associated with Dravet syndrome to include pediatric patients 6 months to less than 2 years of age weighing 7 kg or more

citations.quote: These Prior Approval sNDAs provide for the expansion of the use of Diacomit for the treatment of seizures associated with Dravet syndrome in patients taking clobazam to include pediatric patients who are 6 months to less than 2 years of age and weighing 7 kg or more.

orphan_indication.text: Granted orphan designation for the treatment of Dravet syndrome (orphan designation number 08-2661) on October 30, 2008.

citations.quote: STP was granted orphan designation for the treatment of Dravet syndrome by the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) (orphan designation number 08-2661) on October 30, 2008
Priority or Standard	Priority

summary.text: Stiripentol (Diacomit), a new molecular entity, received Priority review and had FDA orphan drug designation for Dravet syndrome. It was approved first cycle based on two randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trials (STICLO France and STICLO Italy) in patients taking clobazam; because of the orphan designation, PREA pediatric assessment was not triggered.
